source.campaign_title_visible: Have Items to Sell? Turn Your Items Into Cash.

visual_read.visual_hierarchy: Typeset serif wordmark top-left with 'The Smarter Way to Sell.' → 'Have Items to Sell?' (large navy serif, title case) → red rule → 'Turn Your Items Into Cash.' → support sentence → four outline-icon benefit rows → red CTA 'Start Your Auction Today →' → navy band with three numbered steps and 'You Can Do This.' script → footer strip 'Real People. Real Support. Real Results.' Merchandise fills the right two-thirds and rises behind the headline.
visual_read.merchandise_treatment: A believable living-room vignette: china cabinet at the back, leather wingback chair with a patterned cushion, table lamp, an open cardboard box lettered 'Turn Your Items Into Cash.', gilt landscape, bronze horse, silver tea set, book stack with category spines, blue-and-white vase, mantel clock, trunk with a bronze dog, red toy truck, patterned bowl, rug. Objects rest on a table and the floor; the cabinet is behind; scale is plausible.
visual_read.composition_style: Left copy column over a light haze fading into a warm interior on the right; merchandise rises to the top edge behind the headline; navy band closes.
visual_read.typography_treatment: Title-case serif headline stack (navy) with a red rule; sans support and benefit rows; script accents in navy with red underlines; small-caps footer.
visual_read.branding_hierarchy: Advantage.Bid leads (typeset wordmark — see logo note); 'ADVANTAGE.BID' repeated under the CTA; band script; no seller.
visual_read.cta_treatment: One red button 'Start Your Auction Today →' with the URL beneath.
visual_read.footer_treatment: Navy band (three steps + script) then a light footer strip with a three-part tagline.
visual_read.photographic_style: Image-model rendered warm interior, soft window light; merchandise photoreal.
visual_read.environmental_staged_composition: Editorial room: cabinet (rear), chair (anchor), table with grouped small objects (surface), rug (ground).

strongest_attributes: Seller acquisition that is merchandise-led, warm and aspirational — it does not look like software advertising
One clear headline question with a one-line answer beneath it
Navy authority + red attention on a light foundation; merchandise supplies the rest of the colour
Physically believable staging: chair grounded, cabinet behind, small objects on a real surface
transferable_lessons: Acquisition creative may be visually rich when ONE headline dominates and every other block is subordinate and organised (benefit rows, step band)
Question headline + answer sub-headline is an approved acquisition structure
Light foundation with a warm interior on one side is within the Owner's 'light' preference
Red for the rule, the CTA and script underlines; navy for the headline and the band
A cardboard box as a 'your items' device is an approved narrative prop (representative, no claim)
do_not_generalize: The typeset serif 'Advantage.Bid™' wordmark — not an approved logo; production composites the official asset

The collaborator's prop set (bronze horse, blue-and-white vase, category books, red truck) — The collaborator's set repeats a bronze rearing horse, a blue-and-white vase, a stack of books with category-name spines, a gilt landscape, a laptop showing the logo and a handwritten script phrase on a mug/board/box. These are the collaborator's props, not required objects; the engine must not learn them as a checklist.
Nine copy blocks as a default — this is the ceiling of the ACQUISITION_RICH profile, not the target
'Keep More of the Proceeds' and the 'in minutes' promise — claims requiring production truth
Handwritten phrase on the box — scene accent only

text_density_assessment.why_it_works_here: Every block sits in a fixed slot and the headline is three times the size of anything else; the merchandise still holds more than half the canvas.
text_density_assessment.advantage_bid_budget_note: Defines the ACQUISITION_RICH ceiling (9 blocks in structured slots). The Owner's stated preference for fast comprehension means the 5-block variant remains the feed default; the proving ground tests both.

composition_assessment.spatial_logic: Room: cabinet on the wall plane behind, chair and table on the floor, small objects on the table, rug under.
composition_assessment.gravity_and_grounding: All furniture grounded; box on the floor; small objects supported.
composition_assessment.depth: Three planes with meaningful overlaps (objects in front of chair, chair in front of cabinet).
composition_assessment.scale_strategy: Chair and cabinet as anchors; table objects at believable scale; the toy truck reads as a toy.
composition_assessment.edge_handling: Cabinet exits the top; trunk exits the right; nothing identifying cut.

avoid_for: any campaign where copy must be minimal

provenance.analysis_method: Direct visual inspection at full resolution; pixel statistics computed from the file; est_* are visual estimates; text transcribed from the image and classified.
